title: Research and indicators
headline: We propose to measure Gen Z and young adults by survey (ages 20–29) and member data (18–29), with baselines by 31 March 2027 to set targets against our data.

methods.what: 1,500 respondents aged 20+, 300 per centre, weighted to footfall

notes: We define Gen Z and young adults as ages 18 to 29. Our survey reaches only people aged 20 and over, the age of majority, so it measures 20 to 29; member data cover active members 18 to 29. We found no CPN age split of visits, so we set a baseline by 31 March 2027. The only published comparator, 14.7 percent for ages 13 to 24, is another band. Four indicators track proposed targets.
